title: scenario-aware-fallback-and-rollforward-lifecycle-adapter
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Opt-in lifecycle adapter that enables scenario-driven automatic rollbacks and rollforwards for canaries, A/B slices and shadow traffic; includes simulation harness and telemetry hooks.
description:
Summary: Implements a scenario-aware lifecycle adapter that evaluates canary/A-B/shadow experiments against configurable scenario analyzers and drives automatic rollback or rollforward decisions.
Motivation: existing rollout controllers make decisions based on static thresholds (latency p95, error rate). Many regressions are scenario-specific (e.g., long-tail latency on high-token prompts, semantic degradation on certain user cohorts) and require richer decision logic plus simulated "what-if" execution before automated actions.
This PR introduces: 1) a lifecycle adapter that plugs into the existing rollout engine and accepts a set of scenario analyzers (plug-ins that return a risk score and root-cause tags), 2) a lightweight simulation harness to run rollout decisions against recent traffic snapshots, 3) telemetry and trace hooks to expose scenario-level metrics to Console and alerting, 4) UI/CLI flags to opt a rollout into "scenario-mode" (opt-in by default), 5) safety gates: mandatory dry-run for the first 2 promotions, decay window for quick re-promote, and manual-latch override.
Design highlights:
- Adapter API: lifecycle policies can reference analyzers by name and configure thresholds (warn_level, abort_level, recheck_interval). The adapter evaluates the analyzers' combined risk and emits structured decisions: allow, warn, abort, or schedule-rollforward.
- Scenario analyzers: included two reference analyzers in this change: token-length-tail (samples long prompts and computes p99-increase) and semantic-drift (per-cohort generation-quality regression via eval harness). They are extensible via a simple Python contract.
- Simulation harness: replays a snapshot of recent traffic (configurable window) through the proposed rollout plan to estimate impact on latency, KV-cache hits, and cost. Simulation runs are recorded as telemetry events and can be promoted to the Console dry-run timeline.
- Safety: when an analyzer returns abort, the adapter can automatically quarantine the new variant to shadow lanes and revert traffic to the previous stable model; automatic rollforwards are only allowed if the simulated run shows <=10% cost increase and no p99 degradation beyond configured limits.
Backwards compatibility: rollout engine falls back to the classic threshold-based evaluator when no scenario analyzers are attached. The adapter is behind a feature flag lifecycle.policy.v2.enabled=false by default.
Checklist:
- [x] new adapter implementation in orchestration/runtime
- [x] two reference analyzers (token-length-tail, semantic-drift)
- [x] simulation harness + replay snapshot loader
- [x] telemetry events and Console timeline integration
- [x] CLI flags and API schema updates + validation
- [x] unit tests for adapters and analyzers
- [x] integration tests executing a small canary with simulated traffic
- [x] migration docs and quickstart in docs/rollouts
- [x] rollout safety gating tests
- [x] added e2e smoke test in perf-canary suite
Testing: local unit/integration runs, CI matrix covered go unit tests, python analyzers linting, and a simulated E2E run in the perf-canary job. We ran a dry-run simulation on real traffic snapshot (2026-01-30) to validate heuristics; results attached to CI artifact.
Known limitations:
- semantic-drift analyzer uses a small golden promptset by default; customers with bespoke prompts should supply their own eval sets for best results
- simulation relies on a sampled, not full, traffic snapshot; extreme tail behaviors can be underrepresented
- rollout decisions are probabilistic; the adapter surfaces a confidence score but does not guarantee zero false positives
Rollout plan for deployment: 1) enable lifecycle.policy.v2.enabled=false by default in main; rollout to staging with the adapter toggled on for internal experiments, 2) after 2 weeks of staging smoke runs and a single on-call rehearsal, flip the flag for a small set of customers (beta), 3) add a guardrail requiring dry-run pass before enabling auto-abort for all customers.
Migration notes: no config changes required for existing policies. New schema validated server-side; older policies continue to work.
Impact to customers: opt-in feature; minimal risk.
Related: Linear ENG-4821 (scenario analyzers), ENG-4999 (simulation harness).

review_comments: Diego Marin: Overall approach LGTM. A few concerns: make sure the analyzer contract prevents blocking RPCs in the runtime path. Can we run analyzers async and surface a cached score?

Aisha Patel: Good point — analyzers run in a bounded worker pool; runtime path uses last-known score and triggers re-evaluation in the background. Updated adapter to return stale_ok when score_age < configured_ttl.
Priya Sharma: We need clearer CPI metrics emitted for simulation runs. Add simulated-cost, sim-latency-95, sim-p99 to telemetry payloads.
Aisha Patel: Added sim-* fields and added the fields to the Console dry-run timeline mapping.
Lara McConnell: Tests look thorough. One request: add a small negative test where simulation indicates large KV-cache regression and ensure the adapter aborts.
Aisha Patel: Added integration case with synthetic cache-unfriendly traffic; adapter aborts and quarantines as expected.
Priya Sharma (approval): Approved after CI green and two nits addressed.
Diego Marin (approval): Approved and left a follow-up to expand analyzer docs in the next PR.
